author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Former U.S. Sen. John E. Sununu won New Hampshire’s Republican Senate primary Tuesday, earning a place in the November race for the seat Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen is leaving after three terms.

New Hampshire Public Radio reported that Sununu had 70% of the vote to Scott Brown’s 25% as of 8:20 p.m., with 16% counted. The figures were preliminary, but NHPR reported that Republican voters had selected Sununu as their nominee.

Sununu previously represented New Hampshire in the Senate from 2003 to 2009 and served one term in the U.S. House before that. Brown, a former Massachusetts senator, had also sought a New Hampshire Senate seat in 2014.

Sununu will face Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas, who won his party’s primary Tuesday. The matchup gives voters a choice between two candidates with federal experience and puts New Hampshire at the center of the national fight for Senate control. Final totals remain subject to the state’s official canvass.
dek: The former senator defeated Scott Brown and will face Democrat Chris Pappas for New Hampshire’s open U.S. Senate seat.
headline: John E. Sununu wins New Hampshire Republican Senate primary
